title: Pizza with extra meat and extra vegetables, medium crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with extra meat and extra vegetables on a medium crust is a classic Italian pizza enriched with additional portions of meat (such as ham, sausage, or chicken) and a variety of vegetables (tomatoes, bell peppers, onions, mushrooms). The medium‑thick dough provides a balance between a crisp edge and a soft interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The meat‑and‑vegetable combo makes this pizza more filling and nutritionally dense.
Medium crust is typically baked at 220‑250 °C, yielding a golden‑brown crust.
Traditionally the pizza is served hot right out of the oven so the cheese stays stretchy.
Variations may include different cheeses such as mozzarella, parmesan, or cheddar.
Pizzas with extra toppings are often ordered in pizzerias as a “premium combo.”

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The added meat provides a substantial amount of high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables contribute vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium and fiber, supporting immunity and digestion.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Carbohydrates from the dough, fats from the cheese, and protein from the meat give lasting satiety.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and bell peppers contain lycopene and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Protein from meat combined with dough carbs aids muscle recovery after exercise.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Extra meat and cheese increase the calorie count, so portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Processed meats and some cheeses can be high in salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Large amounts of cheese and meat raise saturated fat intake, potentially affecting cholesterol levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into serving pieces and enjoy it hot. Fresh basil or arugula added after baking enhances aroma. Optionally drizzle with hot sauce or olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore a crispy crust.
